lots.guide_summary: Every entry is a SOLD hammer price at Gowans (premium extra). No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence was found. Close multi-piece Le Creuset lots made $125 to $390, and single genuine casseroles made $152 to $360. If any piece is not genuine, the floor is an unbranded enamel casserole at $50 and a plain grill pan at $45. AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Keep: the lowest close SOLD with more than one bid and photos checked is $150 (lot 432912, one Le Creuset casserole plus Taiwan skillets, so less than this lot). 150 / 1.198 = 125.2, rounded down to $125 (all-in $149.75). The one-bid $125 lot 373057 was not used because its contents are unknown. Flip: likely resale about $240, between the $150 and $390 close results. The casserole alone is worth about $150 to $180, and the grill pan and chipped saucepan add perhaps $60 to $90. Less 10% selling fees (eBay or a local auction; Marketplace would be free) = $216. No outbound postage, since heavy cast iron sells as local pickup. 216 / 2.396 = 90.2, rounded down to $90.
lots.confidence_reason: The Le Creuset styling is convincing: an oval lid with concentric rings and raised lettering, a round logo boss on the grill pan, and a flame-colour saucepan. But no base mark or lid lettering can be read in the single photo, so the brand rests on the Gowans title and design cues. The SOLD evidence itself is good: several Gowans results opened, and photos of 4 compared.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 13 researcher figures matched the API exactly (price, bids, date). I checked the photos for 366033 and 432912. 432912 includes Taiwan-made skillets, so it is a lower comparison. Added 408809 (green casserole, $360) as a category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Lid lettering is partly visible but not readable even enlarged. The grill pan logo boss is the round Le Creuset style. The orange saucepan has several chips and rust spots on the outside enamel near the rim. The casserole lid is worn and the blue has dulled. The grill pan cooking surface is dark and used. No base marks are shown. The lot already had 4 bids when fetched.
lots.condition: Used. The casserole looks sound but worn. The saucepan has chips with rust in the outside enamel. The grill pan is seasoned and used. Interiors are not fully visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the base marks on all three pieces (Le Creuset, size number, made in France), the size of the oval casserole, and whether the interior enamel of the casserole and saucepan is chipped or crazed?
